nora: FYI the Go generator sample leaks goroutines when a caller cancels mid-stream. repro: start generator, cancel ctx after first chunk, pprof shows a goroutine stuck in handshakeLoop.

ben: i repro'd it. looks like ackCh isn't closed on ctx.Done().

ashwin: can you paste the minimal snippet?

nora: sure:
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
iter := client.Generator(ctx, req)
go func() { time.Sleep(50*time.Millisecond); cancel() }()
for iter.Next() { _ = iter.Token() }
log.Println("err:", iter.Err())
```

chris: ugh. small API suggestion: make iterator implement io.Closer so samples can `defer iter.Close()` and we get deterministic cleanup.

ben: agree. i'll add io.Closer + a sync.Once internal cleanup to avoid double-close races. also add ForEach(ctx, fn) convenience wrapper to reduce Next/Err misuse.

ashwin: prefer runtime handle ctx cancellation automatically, but ForEach + Close are good safeguards. ensure Dedicated/private adapters reuse the same cleanup helper.

dev-bot: Created issue #371: https://github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/issues/371

nora: tests: unit for handshake close once, integration that cancels after first token and asserts goroutine count returns to baseline. CI note: run integration without race detector.

ben: i'll open a draft PR with the changes and tests, will ping here.

chris: thanks. will review and audit other handshake paths once PR is up. :thumbsup:
